messages:
incident-bot: PAGER OPEN — INC-2026-03-15-451. High error rate (503) from embeddings workers in eu-west-1. Alert: 50% errors, p95 latency 1200ms. First seen 6823459999. Link: https://redwood.internal/alerts/INC-2026-03-15-451

Alex: grabbing this — I'm primary. quick glance: kube events show OOMKills on embed-ingester pods. @Mira you're secondary for this shift.

Mira: on standby. i'll handle customer comms if this becomes a customer impact. which customers are hit? :eyes:

Sam: saw consistent `OOMKilled` for embed-ingester-3 and -5. kube events snippet: `Warning  OOMKilling  2m (x3 over 5m)  kubelet  OOMKilled process=kv_cache_writer`

Priya: customer-facing: acme-inc and studyhub reported 503s around 10:20 UTC. CS has been messaged for acme-inc. studyhub contact is queued.

Alex: quick plan: 1) reduce concurrency for embed-ingesters (scale HPA down) 2) cordon+drain suspected node embed-node-7 3) check if yesterday's quantization change correlates with memory spike (if yes, revert canary). Executing commands now.

Jordan: dashboard: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/embed-oom (p95 and error-rate). autoscaler shows frequent scale ups -> down cycles in last 15m. Suggest adding cooldown if we see thrash.

Sam: running cordon+drain now: `kubectl cordon embed-node-7 && kubectl drain embed-node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — will move pods.

incident-bot: Automated mitigation executed: HPA embed-ingester scaled from 10 -> 4 replicas (action triggered by oncall runbook step).

Alex: I've started a canary revert of the quantization change in eu-west: rolling embed-ingester deployment from v3 -> v2 for canary subset (`kubectl rollout restart deploy/embed-ingester -n prod --selector=canary=true`). Watching memory.

Mira: watching logs. error rate dropping to ~18% and p95 down to 420ms in the last 3m. :thumbsup:

Priya: CS update: acme-inc confirms fewer 503s. studyhub says still some rate-limited requests but improving. keeping both in the loop.

Sam: node drain completed for embed-node-7, pods rescheduled onto embed-node-9/10. No CrashLoopBackOff for new pods so far.

Alex: next diagnostics: capture heap profile and check for leaking goroutines. Commands for runbook: `kubectl logs deploy/embed-ingester -c app | grep KVCache` and for heap: `curl http://<pod-ip>:6060/debug/pprof/heap > heap.pb`

Jordan: linking recent mem metrics and autoscaler events: https://redwood.internal/metrics/embed-mem?from=now-1h&to=now. Looks like memory per-pod jumped after 09:50 UTC correlating with the quantization-change rollout.

incident-bot: NOTE — automated reroute to fallback model pool enabled while canary completes. Requests for eu-west are split 80/20 to fallback.

Alex: status check: errors down to 6%, p95 ~280ms. continuing to monitor. If stable for 30m we'll close pager. Also created ticket INF-2412 to root cause memory increase.

Mira: I can take primary for the next 6h starting 03:00 UTC. Sam will be secondary. Priya will handle CS comms. Jordan to follow up on autoscaler cooldown tomorrow.

Alex: leaving handoff notes for Mira: 1) runbook link: https://redwood.dev/runbooks/embed-oom 2) commands to collect profiles (see above) 3) watch for thrashing in HPA (recommend 5m cooldown, minReplicas 2) 4) customer list: acme-inc, studyhub. Last successful pod image: embed-ingester:v2

Mira: acknowledged. i'll watch for next 2 hours then update status. If error rate creeps >10% re-escalate to Alex.

incident-bot: PAGER RESOLVED — INC-2026-03-15-451 closed at 6823463800. Reason: mitigations (HPA scale down + node drain + canary revert) reduced memory pressure and error rate to <5%. Severity downgraded to Sev2 (monitoring). Link to post-incident ticket: https://redwood.internal/tickets/INF-2412

Alex: final handoff summary (for records): 1) Cause likely memory regression from quantization change — reproduces in staging 2) Immediate mitigation: HPA scaled down, node drained, canary revert 3) Next steps: Jordan to tune autoscaler cooldown, Sam to run memory profiler and attach traces to INF-2412, Priya to close CS loops.

Mira: thanks team. I'll keep watch and ping if anything resurges. :coffee:
